about: Partita, two against two (Torino 1787, «Del giuocare in Partita», pp. 88-90), the game the book calls the proper one of four players: two fixed pairs, partners sit face to face, the cards are cut, dealt and discarded as in Permesso for four (19 cards to each, the dealer puts two away), no one may ever go alone («andar a solo mai e poi mai»), the two partners' points are one heap and the part with more points wins, even by a single unpaired card (pp. 88-90). The Bagatto and the kings may not be put away, the Fool is shown (p. 90). Each winner collects the agreed sum from one of the opponents (p. 90). The sum, the count by four or by two and the lead are our readings; who deals first («Chi coppa meglio») is the book's (p. 89). Marks: [D] documented, [R] our reading, [S] sources silent.

nice1930.cite: F. Cason, «Les jeux de cartes à Nice», Armanac Nissart, Nice, 1930, pp. 277-290

dummett1980.cite: Michael Dummett, The Game of Tarot, London: Duckworth, 1980, chapter XIII «Tarocco in Piedmont and Lombardy», pp. 258-279 (our scan is partial: printed page 268 is missing)

torino1846.cite: L. B., Il giuocatore di tarocchi al tavoliere, part I (Grammatica del giuocatore), Torino, Serra, [1846]

prammatica1846.cite: L. B., Prammatica del giuocatore di tarocchi ossia regole indispensabili per gli amatori di simile passatempo, Torino, Serra, [1846] (separate issue, cover dated 1846, deposited 27 December 1845; reprinted from the same setting, same pages, as part II of Il giuocatore di tarocchi al tavoliere, Torino, Serra, [1846])

perchitarocca1794.cite: Per chi tarocca. Almanacco critico-istruttivo per l'anno 1794, Milano, Luigi Veladini [1793/94]; Biblioteca Trivulziana, Triv M 1542 (the Milanese neighbours of the Turin game; a support, not a source of these rules)

tarocaire1880.cite: C. C. Tarocaire, La partia a taroch an quatr. Regolament e caprissi, Turin, Stamperia Leteraria, 1880

count.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 88: «Partita di Tarocchi è un giuoco tra quattro persone. Giuocano due contra altri due».

direction.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 35, 37: «gli altri sempre a destra procedendo»: play passes to the right. A neighbouring support: Per chi tarocca, Milan, 1794, pp. 6, 36: the first in hand is «primo a destra dello scartante, detto perciò l'eletto».

first_dealer.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 89: «Chi coppa meglio degli altri tre compagni è quegli, che comanda agli altri»; the same passage, second support, Torino [1846], part I, p. 35: he «fa, mischia e scarta egli stesso», «o comanda di fare a chi più gli piace»: the one who cuts best deals himself or names the dealer. Other custom: Dummett 1980, p. 261 (his own account): the cards are drawn and the highest deals first. A third custom: Turin 1880, p. 9: «A cöl ch'ai toca 'l prim onor a mëscia i taroch»: who receives the first honour shuffles. The other custom is printed in the eighteenth century too: Per chi tarocca, Milan, 1794, pp. 12-13: «Quelli al quale sarà toccata la carta migliore dovrà incominciare a far le carte».

cut_by.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 58 (Permesso, said before the deal): «ed a sinistra coppati»; who cuts is not named. Read with the general rule of pp. 16-18 as the player on the dealer's left; other reading: only the direction of the cut is meant. Turin 1880, pp. 9-10: «ai dà a cöpè a cöl ch'as treuva a sinistra»: the dealer gives the cut to the player on his left.

cut_min.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 16: «Una carta sola non si può coppare»: the page forbids only a cut of one card; that each part keeps at least two cards is our reading.

dealer_rotation.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 70: after a hand that «si deve ripigliar da capo» «tocca al compagno appresso a mischiare, e dar i Tarocchi»: the next player deals; the book names no other change of dealer, and «appresso» is read in the direction of play (to the right).

seating.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 89: «I due, che sono insieme, sederannosi incontra … e gli altri due sederanno similmente». Who is with whom is decided «dando i posti» (p. 88, how is not said; Dummett 1980, p. 261: by drawing cards, the two highest together). The same custom printed in the eighteenth century: Per chi tarocca, Milan, 1794, p. 13: the dealer «avrà per compagno quelli al quale sarà toccata la seconda carta vincente».

mode.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 88: «Giuocano due contra altri due. Dando i posti, si decide chi debb'essere insieme».

pool.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 89: «I due giuocatori compagni, conteranno i punti … di due mucchj un solo mucchio».

signals.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 73: knocks and signs are barred «a qualunque altro giuoco di Tarocchi». Later customs, not followed: Turin 1880, p. 7: «I re a valo sinch pönt e as marco batend slà taoula»: the partners signal by knocking; p. 10: a trump is called by a knock before the trick is gathered; p. 11: a sign out of time is punished like a revoke (p. 10); p. 11 names the sign after one's own card. Dummett 1980, p. 259 gives signals after the rules of 1830. The neighbours bar them as well: Per chi tarocca, Milan, 1794, p. 27: neither «battere giuocando la carta in segno d'invito» nor «fare dei segni al compagno»; the fine there is agreed, and «one game» (Manfridio) is too much (p. 11).

deck.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 89: dealt «come al giuoco di Permesso in quattro persone»: 4 × 19 + 2 = 78.

trump_order.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 9-10, 13: the trionfi rank by their printed numbers, with the Angel XX above the World XXI («l'usanza, che in questo caso fa legge»); checked on the scan on 2 November 2026.

suit_order.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 11-13: swords and batons run 10 down to 1, cups and coins 1 up to 10, the courts above every numeral in the order King, Queen, Knight, Jack; checked on the scan on 2 November 2026.

card_points.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 13-14, 51: king 5, queen 4, knight 3, jack 2, the Angel, the Bagatto and the Fool 5, every other card 1 in the book's numbers; checked on the scan on 2 November 2026. Turin 1880, p. 8: «'L Fol a val quatr pont da chiel sol»: there the Fool is 4 by itself, without three plain cards.

fool_exchange.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 52, 90: «Il Folle si mostra»; the card owed for the Fool is printed for Baronetti (p. 52) and Venticinque (p. 54) and carried over; it is not printed in the Partita pages. Other reading: none.

fool_exchange_card.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 52: «una cartaccia, qualunque gli piaccia».

fool_exchange_to.source: [R] Torino [1846], part I, p. 33 (Venticinque for three): «onde chi ha presa o coperta la mano non abbia ad averne danno»: the plain card for the Fool goes to whoever took the trick; Torino 1787, pp. 77-78 says the same of Permesso for five to seven: «la carta poscia del Folle si dovrà sempre dare a chi ha preso». With pairs a partner who takes the trick keeps the side whole. Carried over (revision 9). Other reading (stood until revision 8): the card goes to the opposing side.

fool_no_tricks.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 21, rule 10, lists among the things to be agreed before the deal whether a player «avendo o il Folle, o lo scarto» loses the «vola»: it supposes that a player with no trick may hold the Fool, so the Fool stays with him. The pages of this game (pp. 88-90) do not say what a player with no trick does with the Fool, and they do not send to p. 50. Our reading: a player with no trick keeps the Fool; an owner without a plain card gives nothing. Other reading (alt give_fool): Prammatica [1846], p. 6: «chi non potesse coprirlo, alla fine della mano è obbligato di cederlo alla parte vincente»; Torino 1880, p. 9 says only that the Fool of a side with no trick may be taken («as peul piesse»); Dummett 1980, p. 259: «if they have won no tricks, they must surrender the Folle». See OPEN_QUESTIONS.md, question 2.

replace.what: the Fool of a player who won no trick: kept or given up

options.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 89: «V'ha chi pretende … debbano le carte a quattro a quattro contarsi»; «o continsi a quattro a quattro, o a due a due, ciò non importa»: the fours are what some require, the book lets either stand; the default is the pairs, the count of the long games (p. 52). Other reading, by four: Turin 1880, p. 7: «tute cöle figure a devo aveie anssema 3 cartine ciascuna», and p. 11: 36 each is a tie («pata»); Dummett 1980, p. 261: «counted in fours … making 72 points altogether» (the two cards of the discard counted as a set of four, «not explicitly stated»), and p. 263; Cason 1930, p. 279: «le nombre total invariable de points du jeu est de 72». Not the default: counted by four the cards left over, the two of the discard, count as an incomplete group (odd_card as_group), so the deck makes 72 and 36 each is a tie; the number 72 itself is not in Turin 1880.
[D] Torino 1787, p. 90: «del convenuto»: the payment is agreed before the deal; the book names no figure; the choices are ours.

hand_size.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 89: «coppando, dando, e scartando, come al giuoco di Permesso in quattro persone», i.e. 19 to each (p. 71).

dealer_extra.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, pp. 40-41: «non se ne scartano che due»; Prammatica [1846], p. 28 (said of Consiglio): «con due di scarto al distributore». Torino 1787, pp. 71, 89: the deal and the discard as at Permesso for four (4 × 19 + 2 = 78).

packets.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 59: the way of dealing is the dealer's, announced before the cut («come al giuoco di Permesso»). Turin 1880, p. 10: «as devo sempre distribuisse tuti 19 i taroch d'seguit»; if «d'seguit» means one packet of 19, that is another custom (uncertain reading).

packets_announced.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 59: announced before the cut.

order.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 59: «principiando sempre da tua destra».

phases.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 89: the dealer «scarta» as at Permesso for four. Only the dealer sees the discard (view.piles.discard); a neighbouring support, Per chi tarocca, Milan, 1794, pp. 24-25: «lo scartante comunicherà al compagno secretamente li punti scartati, perderà dieci punti».

who.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 89: «o fa, mischia, e scarta egli stesso»: the dealer discards.

count.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 71, 89: two, as at Permesso for four.

count_mode.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, pp. 36, 40-41: «Si scartano due sole carte»; «perchè due sole ne sovrabbondano». A neighbouring support: Per chi tarocca, Milan, 1794, p. 23: «o che scarti una sol carta, o più di due perde dieci punti».

discard_honours_barred.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 90: «Il Folle si mostra, Bagatto non iscartasi, … secondo è stato detto di sopra»: the kings and the Bagatto are named, the Angel and the Fool are not; «secondo è stato detto di sopra» sends to rule 38 (p. 34), where all honours are barred. Other reading: only the Bagatto and the kings (the Angel and the Fool may then be put away; the list «barred» keeps the Bagatto and the kings barred in both readings).

barred.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 90: «Bagatto non iscartasi, nè alcun Re».

allowed_exceptions.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 34 (rule 38): «eccetto che Bagatto sia solo, senza il Folle»: «solo» is read as the only trump of the hand, as Dummett 1980, p. 259 reads this rule («neither the Folle nor any other trump»). Revision 1 read it as «holding no Fool». Page 90 says flatly «Bagatto non iscartasi». Other reading: no exception, as the rules of 1830 have it (Dummett, p. 259). Turin 1880, p. 9 keeps the exception for Partita of four: «s'a l'è mach sol, e nen mai quand a iè 'l Fol ansema»; what «sol» means it does not say.

counts_for.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 21, rule 10 (for every game), lists among the things to be agreed before the deal whether a player «avendo o il Folle, o lo scarto» loses the «vola»: it supposes that a player with no trick may keep his discard, and no Turin book prints the contrary for a game with one discard. Pages 88-90 do not say whose points the discard joins; ours: the dealer's side. Other reading: a side with no trick gives the discard to the taker of the last trick. That a player with no trick loses his discard is printed only in Prammatica [1846], pp. 24-25, n. 15 «Mittigati in due collo scarto compito», a game for two: «La così detta vola … perde i punti dei due scarti, tanto piccolo che grande», and the Fool with them («e con essi anche il Folle»); the page does not say who gains them. Dummett 1980, p. 259 gives a rule for it («they must surrender the discarded cards to the player or side winning the last trick») and names no source. See OPEN_QUESTIONS.md, question 1.

replace.what: the discard of a player who won no trick: kept or lost

announce.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 60: after «ho scartato» the discard cannot change. A later custom, not followed: Turin 1880, p. 11: «Cöl ch'a scarta a l'è sempre padron d'cambiè l'scart»: the discard may be changed until a card is played.

first_leader.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 35 (general rule): «Chi è a destra di chi dà, comincia»; the Partita pages do not say who leads, and nobody goes alone (p. 89). A neighbouring support: Per chi tarocca, Milan, 1794, p. 6: «primo a destra dello scartante», and p. 36: «La prima giuocata di chi ha la letta».

next_leader.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 37: «Colui, che or ultimo ha preso la mano … deve essere il primo a giuocare».

follow_suit.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 35: «debbon rispondere con carte della medesima sequenza».

must_trump.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, p. 36, for Partita and «anche negli altri giuochi»: «si risponderà e prenderà con un Trionfo». Torino 1787, p. 36 only shows it. Torino 1787, p. 49 (Baronetti) prints the same duty: «se non ho carte della medesima sequenza prendo con Trionfi». A neighbouring support: Per chi tarocca, Milan, 1794, p. 43: «e non avendo tarocchi, deve dare le carte di un altro palo».

must_overtrump.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 36-37: a trionfo is answered with a trionfo and the higher takes; the book states no duty to beat the trump on the table (the fourth player «mette giù un Trionfo maggior» in the example, as a choice).

fool_may_lead.source: [S] Ours: the book does not say whether the Fool may be led; as in Venticinque (and p. 77 «solamente si mostra, quando cada in acconcio») it may be shown at any turn. Turin 1880, p. 8: «as peul passesse quand a conven d'pì»: the Fool is played when it suits, the lead not named.

count_unit.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 88-90: a single unpaired card decides («ancorchè scompagnata»); the half-point arithmetic of pp. 51-52 is carried over.

group.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 89: «o continsi a quattro a quattro, o a due a due, ciò non importa»: by two, when the table agrees on pairs (option group).

odd_card.source: [R] Its value, half a point for a plain card, is our reading (Dummett 1980, p. 261, counts the pack as 91 in twos). That an unpaired card counts at all is [D] Torino 1787, p. 90: «Una carta sola, che … di più di … dar loro la partita».

fool_card.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 88-90 are silent on the Fool's card; read after the later document of the same game, Turin 1880, p. 8: «'L Fol a val quatr pont da chiel sol»: the Fool counts with its owner (there 4 by itself, without three plain cards).

count_unit.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 88-90: a single unpaired card decides («ancorchè scompagnata»); the half-point arithmetic of pp. 51-52 is carried over.

group.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 89: «o continsi a quattro a quattro, o a due a due, ciò non importa»: by four, when the table agrees on fours (option group).

odd_card.source: [R] Dummett 1980, pp. 261, 263: counted in fours the cards make 72 points; the cards left over are a short group, so the two odd cards of the discard count in full; Nice 1930, p. 279; Turin 1880, p. 11: 36 each is a tie («pata»). Torino 1787, p. 90 names only «Una carta sola» left over.

fool_card.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 88-90 are silent on the Fool's card; read after the later document of the same game, Turin 1880, p. 8: «'L Fol a val quatr pont da chiel sol»: the Fool counts with its owner (there 4 by itself, without three plain cards).

winner.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 89-90: «La parte, che fa più punti, è quella, che vince».

tie.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 89-90 do not say what equal points are worth; read after the later document of the same game, Turin 1880, p. 11: «se tute döi le part a n'an fane mach tranteses a resta pata»: at 36 each no one pays. So Dummett 1980, p. 261: «if both sides have 36 points, neither pays».

game_points.source: [S] Torino 1787, p. 90 names no game points; the hand is settled in stakes.

unit.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 90: «del convenuto»: the agreed sum.

mode.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 90: «Vincendo, io mi farò pagare del convenuto … dall'altro similmente esigerai la tua vincita».

amount.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 90: «del convenuto»; the book names no figure. Dummett 1980, p. 261 gives an «onoranza» of 10 (not printed in the book).

variants.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, p. 36: «La partita ordinariamente si finisce in quattro scarti». Paid once, at the end of the four deals (match.payout). Second support: Torino 1787, p. 97, said of Consiglio: «presso altri è chi fa più punti in tutto il giro».

kind.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, p. 36: «La partita ordinariamente si finisce in quattro scarti».

hands.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, p. 36: «La partita ordinariamente si finisce in quattro scarti».

tiebreak.source: [R] Torino [1846], part I, pp. 35-36: the points are counted «sul fine della partita»; game points are none, so this key decides the variant: the side with more card points over the four hands wins, equal totals are a draw (at 36 the partita «rimane in pace», Prammatica [1846], p. 15).

payout.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, pp. 35-36: the points of the four deals are counted «sul fine della partita» and the partita is paid once at its end; Prammatica [1846], p. 15: at equal totals the partita «rimane in pace», nobody pays. [S] The size is ours: it is reckoned as the payment of one deal (settle: pair_split, «del convenuto», 1787, p. 90), one stake from each seat of the losing pair; no payment after each deal in this variant.

kind.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 90: each winner collects «del convenuto» from one opponent; when is not said, and the marche are settled after every deal (ours). The match ends after one round of dealers (match.dealer_rounds); the greatest balance wins, equal balances are a draw («pace», the word of Prammatica [1846], p. 15).

replace.what: one stake at the end of the partita, or the marche after every deal

dealer_rounds.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, p. 36: «La partita ordinariamente si finisce in quattro scarti», so that each of the four discards in turn: one round of dealers, four deals. [S] The marche are still settled after every deal: Torino 1787, p. 90 prints the payment («del convenuto»), not when it is made. Other custom: the partita is decided by the sum of the points of the four deals and one stake is paid at its end (Torino [1846], part I, pp. 35-36: «contando sul fine della partita i punti fatti»; Prammatica [1846], p. 15: at 36 the partita «rimane in pace»); played as the variant «four_deals» (match.payout). The table may also agree on two or three rounds (ours; the book leaves stakes to agreement before the deal, p. 21).

effect.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 90: «Chi rinega, paga secondo le regole sovradette», i.e. rule 35 (pp. 33-34; p. 38 sends to it): the game to all; [S] whether the offender's partner shares the payment is not said. The engine refuses a card that does not follow suit.

[D] Torino 1787, p. 73: «costui pagherà la partita semplice a tutti … giuocare, o far cessare il giuoco»; named for Permesso for three, four and five and for Chiamare il Re (and «a qualunque altro giuoco di Tarocchi»). [R] who the offender may be is not said (any player); the table cannot see a knock, so only the rules page tells it.

play.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 90: «Si procura sempre di sostenere il compagno, … in mano miglior giuoco di noi».

left_out.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 89: «non sarà lecito poi, giuocando in Partita, di andar a solo mai».
left_out.why: The table has no lone contract at Partita, so nobody can go alone; no penalty is needed.

left_out.source: [R] Dummett 1980, p. 261 (his guesses, not printed in the book): a double payment when the loser has fewer than 18 points, a triple for a vola, an extra for each five points.
left_out.why: Not in the 1787 book; the stake is the agreed simple sum.

left_out.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 34 (rule 38): the Fool may be put away «in un sol caso … guadagnar la partita vola»; Turin 1880, p. 9: «as peul dcò scartesse quand ch'a iè la certëssa d'fè la vola»; Dummett 1980, p. 259 reads the same.
left_out.why: Vola is not played (open question 13); the exception is not offered.

left_out.source: [D] Per chi tarocca, Milan, 1794 (the neighbours of the Turin game): a revoke costs ten points of the count, «ordinariamente porta la penale di soli dieci punti» (p. 21); no trump may be discarded, «Se chi scarta scartasse un onore, od un tarocco perderà dieci punti» (pp. 23-24), while a king in the discard is ordinary play (p. 36); the partners change in the course of an evening (pp. 13, 31); one card turned by accident in the deal is no misdeal, «si volta per accidente una carta, non si va a monte» (p. 17).
left_out.why: Customs of Milan, not of Turin: the book of 1787 decides for its own games (a revoke pays the simple game to all, p. 33; kings may not be discarded, p. 90; the pairs are fixed, p. 88). Recorded so that the difference is seen; not played.

left_out.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 89: whoever cuts best of the other three «comanda agli altri di fare»: he deals himself («o fa, mischia, e scarta egli stesso») or tells whom he likes to deal; Torino [1846], part I, p. 35, says the same.
left_out.why: Not played: the table has no choice for the winner of the cut; the first dealer is the one the table gives (seats.first_dealer best_cut says only that he is the one who cut best). Revision 11.
